title: Task Inputs, Outputs, Incrementality, and Determinism

scout.purpose: Turn task inputs, outputs, incrementality, and determinism into a predictable, testable build-system contract.
scout.realWorldUse: Large Android builds must produce trustworthy variants quickly across developer machines and CI while tooling and module graphs evolve.
scout.outcome: Model the build behaviour, implement it with lazy public APIs, and verify correctness plus performance.

blocks.text: Gradle can skip or reuse work only when a task truthfully declares everything affecting its outputs. Annotate scalar and nested inputs, input files with appropriate path sensitivity and normalisation, output files or directories, and internal properties that do not affect results. Missing an input risks stale incorrect output; declaring irrelevant state causes avoidable misses. A task with no output cannot normally be up to date. The contract is functional: the same declared inputs and implementation should produce equivalent outputs.

blocks.text: Incremental execution tells a task which input files changed so it can update outputs selectively. Up-to-date checks reuse outputs in the current workspace, while the build cache can reuse matching outputs from another execution or machine. These mechanisms share input modelling but solve different reuse scopes. Cacheability additionally requires relocatable, deterministic output: avoid absolute paths, current time, random order, machine-specific metadata and undeclared tools. If nondeterminism is intentional, disable caching and explain why.

blocks.caption: A focused build fragment; its full correctness depends on declared inputs, lifecycle, compatibility and functional evidence.

blocks.text: Design stale-output handling for removed inputs, atomic generation, failure cleanup and concurrent execution. Never write outside declared output locations or mutate source directories. Test a first run, identical rerun, one changed input, removed input, relocated project and FROM_CACHE restoration. Inspect cache keys when hits differ. A fast task returning UP-TO-DATE is not evidence of correctness unless changing every meaningful input invalidates it and unchanged inputs reproduce byte-for-byte compatible results.

Build logic is production infrastructure: it shapes every developer feedback loop and release artifact. Make ownership, inputs, outputs, compatibility, security boundaries, failure messages, metrics and rollback explicit. Prefer public typed APIs, lazy Provider wiring and deterministic isolated tasks. Verify the model through representative local and CI workflows, clean and incremental changes, parallel execution, relocated workspaces, configuration-cache reuse and trusted build-cache restoration. Measure before optimising, then preserve correctness with functional tests and regression budgets. Avoid hidden environment state, internal APIs, task-name guessing, global project mutation, mutable network inputs and credentials in logs or reusable outputs. Record the supported Gradle, AGP, Kotlin, Java and operating-system matrix, and make upgrades controlled experiments with safe rollback evidence. A fast build is valuable only when it produces the right traceable artifact consistently.

blocks.title: Common build trap
blocks.text: Watch carefully for this common failure mode in production: Using the current timestamp in generated JSON while omitting it from inputs makes identical cache keys produce different bytes and poisons shared reuse.

trap_check.mistake: Using the current timestamp in generated JSON while omitting it from inputs makes identical cache keys produce different bytes and poisons shared reuse.
trap_check.why: The build may become eager, stale, nondeterministic, incorrectly variant-aware or unsafe under parallel and cached execution.
trap_check.fix: Use the public model, declare the complete data flow and add a functional regression test.

trap_check.mistake: Optimising a synthetic clean build without measuring the team’s frequent workflow.
trap_check.why: The change can shift cost or complexity without improving developer or CI feedback.
trap_check.fix: Baseline representative workflows and compare controlled before/after critical paths.

challenge_intro.task: Implement a cacheable index task and prove correct outcomes for unchanged, changed, deleted, relocated and restored-from-cache scenarios.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The build behaviour is correct for clean, incremental, parallel and cached paths and has measured evidence, diagnostics and ownership.

recall.prompt: What is the core cacheability invariant?
recall.answer: Equivalent declared inputs and implementation must produce equivalent relocatable outputs without undeclared side effects.

recall.prompt: What makes custom Gradle work trustworthy?
recall.answer: Complete declared inputs and outputs, deterministic isolated execution, lazy wiring, public APIs and functional tests.

recall.prompt: What should precede a build-performance change?
recall.answer: A representative workflow, controlled baseline and evidence locating the critical path or avoidable work.
